recipes.name: PRO Negative 160C
recipes.look: Natural yet vibrant professional color negative, moderate saturation, warm skin tones, mid-2000s film feel.
recipes.notes: Versatile everyday recipe for any time of day or night; emulates Fujicolor PRO 160C. Originally X100VI/GFX100 II only until Reala Ace reached other X-Trans V bodies.

image.alt: Amazing Grace – Glendale, AZ – Fujifilm X100VI – PRO Negative 160C

recipes.name: Easy Reala Ace
recipes.look: Gentle, true-to-life color with soft tonal contrast; clean, modern, neutral Fujifilm rendering.
recipes.notes: By Nathalie Boucry; minimal tweak of default Reala Ace, versatile across subjects, light and environments. Needs Reala Ace (X100VI/X-T50 first, others via firmware).

image.alt: Vintage Shell – Bisbee, AZ – Fujifilm X100VI – Easy Reala Ace Recipe

recipes.name: Fujifilm Negative
recipes.look: Analog-like Fujifilm color negative look, slightly warm, moderate saturation, soft contrast; 2000s pro film vibe.
recipes.notes: Best in sunny daylight; fine in overcast or indoor natural light. Too yellow under artificial light, too cool in shade. Inspired by PRO 160NS.

image.alt: Small Yellow Boat – Clinton, CT – Fujifilm X-T5 – Fujifilm Negative Recipe

recipes.name: Fujicolor Film
recipes.look: Muted, true-to-life printed color negative, low saturation, soft contrast, visible grain; 2000s Fujicolor prints.
recipes.notes: Best in sunny daylight, though handles varied light. True-to-life, not punchy; evokes printed Fujicolor PRO 160S.

image.alt: Rainbows over Philly – Philadelphia, PA – Fujifilm X100VI – Fujicolor Film Recipe

recipes.name: Fujicolor 100 Industrial
recipes.look: Slightly offbeat consumer film color, warm-magenta cast, contrasty, mildly muted; Japanese drugstore film of 2000s-2010s.
recipes.notes: Emulates Japan-only Fujicolor 100 Industrial with tungsten-leaning dyes; shown in natural daylight. Reala Ace version preferred over older PRO Neg. Std adaptation.

image.alt: Lion Fountain - Buckeye, AZ - Fujifilm X100VI - Fujicolor 100 Industrial

recipes.name: Kodak Gold Max 400 Expired
recipes.look: Muted, grainy expired consumer film, faded low-contrast shadows, gentle warmth; 1990s drugstore Kodak print.
recipes.notes: Obvious analog vibe unlike typical JPEGs. Author notes match to real expired film is imperfect given scanning and batch variation.

image.alt: Half Moon Over Central Park – New York City, NY – Fujifilm X100VI – Kodak Gold Max 400 Expired

recipes.name: Pushed Analog
recipes.look: Warm, contrasty, highly saturated push-processed Kodak look with 81A warming filter; punchy analog vibe.
recipes.notes: Best in sunny daylight, also good at dusk/dawn; weaker in overcast and artificial light, results vary by subject. Mimics ISO 100 Kodak pushed one stop with an 81A filter.

recipes.name: Nostalgia Negative
recipes.look: Warm, vintage analog look between Eterna and Classic Chrome, soft shadows, rich amber-tinted color.
recipes.notes: Daylight, midday or golden hour, decent in shade; landscapes, portraits, urban. Avoid indoor artificial light and night. Smooth Skin Effect Off. HEIF disables Clarity; Clarity adds brief post-shot pause.

recipes.name: Timeless Negative
recipes.look: Warm, muted 1970s American color negative, low saturation, bright highlights with open shadows.
recipes.notes: Very versatile; works for many genres and light conditions, day or night. Refines Fujifilm's own Nostalgic Neg. suggestions.

recipes.name: Thommy's Ektachrome
recipes.look: Contrasty slide-film look, rich but natural color, National Geographic-style Ektachrome; classic late-20th-century editorial.
recipes.notes: Best in sunny daylight; also good in overcast, shade and natural-light indoors. Created for portraits; Ektachrome look arose by chance.

image.alt: Reserved – Tucson, AZ – Fujifilm X-T5

recipes.name: Retro Slide
recipes.look: Vivid, contrasty vintage slide film on a light table, saturated Ektachrome/Elite Chrome color, crisp clarity.
recipes.notes: Made for sunny daylight; other light is hit-or-miss (can go too warm or cool). Night sometimes works but not a first choice.

image.alt: Meadow Gold Mack – Tulsa, OK – Fujifilm X-E5 – Retro Slide

recipes.name: Kodak Vision3 250D v2
recipes.look: Cinematic motion-picture film look, high contrast, slightly muted color, cool-green cast with warm shadows.
recipes.notes: Nostalgic Neg. version of the X-Trans IV Eterna-based v1; warmer shadows. Author suggests trying both versions.

image.alt: Layers of Urban Construction - Phoenix, AZ - Fujifilm X-T5 - Kodak Vision3 250D v2

recipes.name: Appalachian Negative
recipes.look: Warm amber-toned nostalgic color negative, saturated, soft highlights, crisp detail; childhood-snapshot Appalachian autumn feel.
recipes.notes: By Logan Ballew, derived from Kodak Portra 400 v2. Recommends a 5% or 10% CineBloom diffusion filter; suits foliage and urban scenes.

recipes.name: Agfa Ultra 100 v2
recipes.look: Vibrant, contrasty expired-film color, slightly warm, saturated but lab-scanned consumer feel; 2000s Agfa.
recipes.notes: Intended for sunny daylight but fine in varied light. Based on limited samples of expired, lab-scanned film; warmer and more vibrant than v1.

image.alt: Yellow Blossoms Along a Fence - Buckeye, AZ - Fujifilm X-T5 - Agfa Ultra 100 v2

recipes.name: Emulsion '86
recipes.look: Warm, saturated mid-1980s Kodak-print nostalgia, soft highlights, deep shadows, heavy grain.
recipes.notes: Good for both sunny daylight and rainy overcast. Inspired by Little House on the Prairie pilot and Expo '86 snapshots.

image.alt: Bobcat on the Beach – Oceanside, CA – Fujifilm X-T5 – "Emulsion '86"

recipes.name: Summer of 1960
recipes.look: High-contrast, warm, saturated aged transparency look, soft sharpness; 1960s magazine color.
recipes.notes: Especially suited to sunny daylight; alright in overcast, shade and natural-light indoors. Emulates 1960 Arizona Highways Ektachrome/Kodachrome pages.

recipes.name: 1976 Kodak
recipes.look: Warm, rich, high-contrast 1970s Kodak color, saturated with deep shadows; Meyerowitz Cape Cod era.
recipes.notes: Versatile across many light situations; may run warm in artificial light. Emulates Joel Meyerowitz's 1976 work; pairs well with vintage lenses.

recipes.name: Nostalgic Air
recipes.look: Soft, airy, natural color with peachy highlights and calm blues; gentle contrast, modern film nostalgia.
recipes.notes: By Hayden Goldsworthy; shines in sun, reliable elsewhere. Recommends slight overexposure and a Tiffen Glimmerglass 1 diffusion filter.

recipes.name: Summer of '59
recipes.look: Warm, faded vintage Kodachrome, amber-tinged, low saturation, soft cinematic contrast; 1950s street color.
recipes.notes: Emulates Saul Leiter's 1950s color (aka Expired Vintage Kodachrome); suits reflections, shooting through glass, layered compositions, shadows. Also works on X-Trans IV, rendering very slightly differently. Formerly early-access, now free.

recipes.name: Summer Sun
recipes.look: Bright, very warm, saturated vintage consumer film, like Kodak Ultra Color with a warming filter.
recipes.notes: Best on bright sunny days, okay when partly sunny. Very warm, so not for every subject or light.

image.alt: Buckeye Motor Hotel – Buckeye, AZ – Fujifilm X-E5 – Summer Sun Recipe

recipes.name: 1970's Summer
recipes.look: Warm, muted Kodak memory color, soft highlights, heavy grain; 1970s American New Color photography.
recipes.notes: Best in sunny daylight, excellent for midday. Evokes 1970s New Color photographers like Eggleston and Shore.

image.alt: Gillespie Dam Bridge – Arlington, AZ – Fujifilm X-T5

recipes.name: 1971 Kodak
recipes.look: Warm yellowish, faded, subdued colors, flattish yet contrasty; aged early-1970s family snapshot prints.
recipes.notes: Mimics aged early-1970s Kodacolor-X prints from a family album. Best in sunny daylight, ideally with vintage or characterful third-party lenses; highlights tend to blow out like the originals.

image.alt: View of the North Rim from the South – Grand Canyon NP, AZ – Fujifilm X-T5 – 1971 Kodak

recipes.name: Nostalgic Americana
recipes.look: Obviously retro, low-contrast, muted warm Americana; faded 1960s-70s magazine print look with heavy grain.
recipes.notes: Inspired by 1960s-70s Arizona Highways Kodachrome/Ektachrome magazine photos; works best in sunny daylight. Low contrast and clarity mimic aged magazine printing.

image.alt: On Top of a Desert Hill – Tucson, AZ – Fujifilm X-T5 – Nostalgic Americana

recipes.name: Kodak Vericolor VPS
recipes.look: Warm, saturated, fairly contrasty late-1970s/early-80s color negative print look with prominent grain.
recipes.notes: Very versatile: sunny daylight, golden hour, overcast, natural indoor light, even some night scenes. Evokes late-1970s Vericolor prints.

recipes.name: Kodak Vericolor III 160
recipes.look: Fairly neutral, soft-contrast professional color negative with gentle saturation; 1980s-90s portrait film feel.
recipes.notes: More neutral Vericolor III rendition developed with Thomas Schwab, without simulated warming filter. Can be slightly too cool in some situations; Kodak Vericolor Warm is the warmer alternative.

image.alt: Frontier Motel & Cafe – Truxton, AZ – Fujifilm X-T5 – Kodak Vericolor III 160

recipes.name: Kodak Vericolor Warm
recipes.look: Warm, softly contrasted professional color negative look, like Vericolor with an 81A warming filter.
recipes.notes: Best for daylight but usable at blue hour and in overcast. Emulates Vericolor III 160/II NPS shot through a warming (81A) filter, possibly with a polarizer.

image.alt: Roadside Memorial – Arlington, AZ – Fujifilm X-T5

recipes.name: Kodak Negative
recipes.look: Vibrant, warm, saturated Kodak consumer negative look with lifted shadows; 1990s snapshot feel.
recipes.notes: Evokes vibrant Kodak color negatives like Ektar 100 or Royal Gold 100. Especially suited to golden hour but works in most light.

recipes.name: California Summer
recipes.look: Warm, vibrant, sun-soaked and nostalgic; soft-contrast summery color negative look for street and architecture.
recipes.notes: Inspired by photographer Preet. Best in sunny daylight, including harsh midday and golden hour; OK in shade; avoid indoor artificial light and night.

image.alt: Orange Twist – Buena Park, CA – Fujifilm X100VI – California Summer

recipes.name: Vibrant Arizona
recipes.look: Warm, vivid, pastel-leaning cinematic color with flattened tones; Wes Anderson desert storybook look.
recipes.notes: Wes Anderson-inspired. Use in sunny daylight; author prefers 16:9 aspect for a cinematic feel. Uses D-Range Priority Strong, so no Highlight/Shadow. X-Trans IV version uses FX Blue Strong.

image.alt: Bookshelf Plant – Buckeye, AZ – Fujifilm X-E4

recipes.name: Indoor Angouleme
recipes.look: Warm amber, soft, low-contrast cinematic interior look with muted colors; retro film-set feel.
recipes.notes: Wes Anderson-inspired (The French Dispatch newspaper office). Designed for artificial and mixed indoor lighting, where it shines. X-Trans IV version uses Eterna instead.

image.alt: Bookshelf Plant – Buckeye, AZ – Fujifilm X-E4

recipes.name: Texas Sun
recipes.look: Warm, colorful, Portra-like Kodak negative vibe with extra vibrancy and punchy grain.
recipes.notes: By Jay Ybarra. Excels in backlit sun, with flash, midday, sunset and blue hour. May be too warm; try 6300K/6100K. On X-Trans IV set FX Blue to Strong.

image.alt: Manhattan Skyline from Central Park – New York City, NY – Fujifilm X100VI – Texas Sun Recipe

recipes.name: Pacific Blues
recipes.look: Bright, airy, saturated with deep blues and lifted shadows; sunny Mediterranean summer film look.
recipes.notes: Emulates Lucy Laucht's Positano Blues; made for summer beaches but works in fog, overcast, deserts, flowers, autumn, portraits. X-Trans IV version uses FX Blue Strong.

recipes.name: Copenhagen Negative
recipes.look: Cool-neutral, high-contrast, saturated Classic Negative look with bright highlights; moody Scandinavian film feel.
recipes.notes: Good in sun, clouds, fog, natural indoor light and golden hour; avoid artificial light/night. Responds well to slight underexposure; watch highlights. Renders slightly differently on X-Trans IV.

image.alt: Baltic View – Greve, Denmark – Fujifilm X-E5 – Copenhagen Negative

recipes.name: Fujicolor Super HG v2
recipes.look: Neutral-to-cool, crisp, moderately saturated Fujicolor consumer negative; late-1980s/90s snapshot look.
recipes.notes: Aims for Super HG 100/200 film. Auto White Priority makes it versatile any time of day or night. Separate X-Trans IV version exists.

image.alt: Boat Shack at Sunset – Tempe, AZ – Fujifilm X-T5 – Fujicolor Super HG v2

recipes.name: Reggie's Superia
recipes.look: Moody, contrasty, grainy Fujicolor Superia-inspired negative look with rich but restrained color.
recipes.notes: By Reggie Ballesteros for portraits across skin tones; best in directional light, leaning into highlights or shadows. No typical exposure comp given by request; judge each shot. Not for X-T3/X-T30.

recipes.name: Fujicolor Superia 100
recipes.look: Fairly low-contrast, nicely colored, nostalgic 1990s-2000s Fujicolor snapshot look; neutral-warm.
recipes.notes: General-purpose for portraits, street, landscapes. Fairly low contrast. Renders very warm under indoor artificial light. X-Trans IV version uses FX Blue Weak.

recipes.name: Reala Ace
recipes.look: Soft, colorful, neutral-cool modern analog look; clean Fujifilm Reala Ace negative feel.
recipes.notes: Soft yet colorful and highly versatile for all subjects and light; blend of Reala 100 and NPS 160 Pulled. On X-Trans IV blues are less deep; X-Pro3/X100V use Highlight -1 or -2.

image.alt: Luxury Among Palms – Laguna Hills, CA – Fujifilm X-T5 – Reala Ace Recipe

recipes.name: Fujicolor Reala 100
recipes.look: Neutral, natural, soft-toned and muted Fujicolor negative; understated 1990s-2000s professional film look.
recipes.notes: Emulates Fujicolor Reala 100, a portrait/wedding film; neutral and natural. Separate X-Trans IV version exists (FX Blue differs).

image.alt: Houses on the Hill – Laguna Beach, CA – Fujifilm X-T5 – Fujicolor Reala 100 Recipe

recipes.name: Superia Xtra 400
recipes.look: Vivid, warm-leaning consumer color negative with punchy contrast and grain; late-1990s snapshot look.
recipes.notes: By Thomas Schwab via side-by-side film comparisons of 1998-era Superia Xtra 400. Versatile for most subjects; film results vary with exposure, development and scanning.

recipes.name: Fujicolor Natura 1600
recipes.look: Muted, soft, low-contrast high-ISO film look with heavy grain and lifted shadows; 2000s Japanese snapshot feel.
recipes.notes: Modeled on Natura 1600 scans; versatile across sunsets, night, overcast and artificial light. Separate X-Trans IV version exists.

recipes.name: Fujicolor Superia 1600
recipes.look: Muted, desaturated, grainy high-ISO color negative with lifted shadows; gritty 2000s film feel.
recipes.notes: Emulates discontinued ultra-high-ISO Superia 1600; best used at ISO 1600-6400. Separate X-Trans IV version exists.

image.alt: Senna Shrub Blossom – Buckeye, AZ – Fujifilm X-T5 – Fujicolor Superia 1600

recipes.name: Classic Amber
recipes.look: Warm amber, contrasty and saturated; like Portra 400 pushed a stop with an 81B warming filter.
recipes.notes: Best in low-contrast, cool light like early-morning forests and shade; also sunrise, daytime, concerts. Can easily get too warm and contrasty; not for every scene. Renders slightly differently on X-Trans IV.

image.alt: Golden Appalachian Light - Gatlinburg, TN - Fujifilm X-T5 - Classic Amber

recipes.name: Kodak Farbwelt 200 Expired
recipes.look: Soft, warm, faded low-saturation expired-film look like hazy old summer snapshots.
recipes.notes: Slight underexposure keeps highlights in check. Designed for X-Trans V and new GFX; usable on X-Trans IV but renders slightly differently.

image.alt: Orange Rocks – Sedona, AZ – Fujifilm GFX100S II – Kodak Farbwelt 200 Expired

recipes.name: Kodak Portra 160 v2
recipes.look: Warm yet natural, gentle-contrast Portra color negative rendering with soft tonality and fine grain.
recipes.notes: Best in sunny light incl. sunrise/sunset and midday; poor for night. DR-P replaces Highlight/Shadow. X-Trans IV: set Color Chrome FX Blue to Strong.

recipes.name: Kodak Portra 400 v2
recipes.look: Warm, golden, moderately saturated professional color-negative look with soft shadows and visible grain.
recipes.notes: A favorite for daylight and especially golden hour. Not ideal under indoor artificial light unless you want very warm images. Separate X-Trans IV version exists.

image.alt: Changing Seasons – Buckeye, AZ – Fujifilm X-T5

recipes.name: Kodak Pro 400
recipes.look: Clean, natural, lightly warm modern color-negative look with soft highlights and moderate saturation.
recipes.notes: Portra 400-inspired; thrives in daylight and handles overcast well, but author calls it hit-or-miss. Requires Reala Ace, so not X-Trans IV compatible.

image.alt: Hillside – Elk, CA – Fujifilm X-T5 – Kodak Pro 400

recipes.name: Kodak Portra 800 v3
recipes.look: Warm, saturated, soft-contrast Kodak negative look with heavy grain, inspired by Peter McKinnon's Portra 800.
recipes.notes: Best in golden-hour and midday light; OK in shade, overcast, natural-light interiors and night; avoid warm artificial light. X-Trans IV: FX Blue Weak; X-Pro3/X100V: Shadow 0.

image.alt: South Rim Sunrise - Grand Canyon NP, AZ - Fujifilm X-T5 - Kodak Portra 800 v3

recipes.name: Kodak Ultramax 400
recipes.look: Punchy, contrasty, saturated consumer-film look with warm cast and coarse grain, 1990s-2000s snapshot feel.
recipes.notes: Highly versatile: daylight, overcast, indoors, night, landscapes, portraits. X-Trans V tweak sets FX Blue Off; separate X-Trans IV version exists.

image.alt: Happiness and Wondering – Gilbert, AZ – Fujifilm X-T5

recipes.name: Kodak Gold 200
recipes.look: Warm, golden, nostalgic consumer-film look with rich color and soft highlights.
recipes.notes: Works best in sunny daylight. X-Trans IV (X-T4, X-S10, X-E4, X-T30 II): FX Blue Weak; not for X100V/X-Pro3. One facsimile of many Gold 200 looks.

recipes.name: Kodak Royal Gold 400
recipes.look: Vibrant, warm, red-leaning 1990s print look with punchy color and vintage character.
recipes.notes: Aims at 1990s-2000s 'memory color' prints, possibly mishandled film. FX Blue Weak on X-Trans V, Strong on X-Trans IV; not X-T3/X-T30. Formerly app-only, now public.

recipes.name: Classic Color
recipes.look: Bright, warm, saturated Kodak color-negative look with soft shadows and gentle grain.
recipes.notes: Best in sunny daylight, sometimes fine elsewhere. FX Blue Weak on X-Trans V, Strong on X-Trans IV. Resembles Portra 400 v3 / old Portra 400 VC.

image.alt: Bell Tower – Tumacacori, AZ – Fujifilm X-T5 – Classic Color

recipes.name: Kodachrome 64
recipes.look: Contrasty, warm slide-film look with deep cyan-blue skies, rich reds and crisp detail.
recipes.notes: X-Trans V tweak of the X-Trans IV Kodachrome 64 recipe (FX Blue Off, Shadow +0.5) since X-Trans V renders blue deeper. Emulates 1974-2009 era Kodachrome 64.

image.alt: Girl on Swing – Buckeye, AZ – Fujifilm X-T5

recipes.name: Kodachrome 25
recipes.look: Sharp, grainless, crisp 1970s slide-film look with natural but rich color and firm contrast.
recipes.notes: X-Trans V version of the X-Trans IV recipe with FX Blue reduced to Weak. Mimics very sharp, low-ISO Kodachrome 25 slide film; ISO capped at 1600.

recipes.name: Kodacolor VR 200
recipes.look: Faded, low-saturation, high-contrast 1980s print look, like 40-year-old poorly stored snapshots.
recipes.notes: Retro look, not an everyday recipe. X-Trans IV (X-T4, X-S10, X-E4, X-T30 II, GFX100S): set FX Blue to Strong.

image.alt: Coastal Arches – Charleston, SC – Fujifilm X-S20 – Kodacolor VR 200 – Photo by Jonathan Roesch

recipes.name: Kodak Ektachrome E100VS v1
recipes.look: Vivid, warm slide-film color, slightly less vibrant than Velvia, with contrast and visible grain.
recipes.notes: ChatGPT-created recipe; versatile via Auto WB and DR400. Lower exposure for deeper blues/reds, higher for lighter, warmer colors. X-Trans III: ignore FX Blue, grain size, Clarity.

image.alt: Garden Apex – Buckeye, AZ – Fujifilm X-T5 – Kodak Ektachrome E100VS v2

recipes.name: Kodak Ektachrome E100VS v2
recipes.look: Saturated, contrasty warm transparency look with bold reds and blues, close to real E100VS slides.
recipes.notes: Author's closer E100VS match; less versatile than v1, watch highlights to avoid clipping. Not for X-T3, X-T30, X-Pro3 or X100V.

image.alt: Garden Apex – Buckeye, AZ – Fujifilm X-T5 – Kodak Ektachrome E100VS v2

recipes.name: Classic Retro
recipes.look: Faded, contrasty 1980s slide look, muted color, like old Ektachrome 400 or expired surplus film.
recipes.notes: Underexposure is key to the aesthetic; avoid clipping highlights. Built for fifth-gen X-Trans and newer GFX; renders differently on X-Trans IV Classic Negative cameras.

image.alt: Downtown Austin – Austin, TX – Fujifilm X-E5 – Classic Retro

recipes.name: Vivid Velvia
recipes.look: Bold, highly saturated Velvia landscape color with controlled contrast and crisp, punchy rendering.
recipes.notes: Sits between two existing Velvia recipes. Good for colorful landscapes and works at night; not a good choice for portraits.

recipes.name: Vivid Chrome
recipes.look: Punchy, vibrant yet restrained slide-film color with moderate contrast and slight warmth.
recipes.notes: Works best in sunny daylight, fine at night with suitable light. Aimed at colorful landscape and travel photos. Compatible with X-T4, X-S10, X-E4, X-T30 II too.

image.alt: Flower Farm – Buellton, CA – Fujifilm GFX100S II – Vivid Chrome

recipes.name: Provia Positive
recipes.look: Vibrant, saturated vintage color-transparency look with gentle contrast and visible grain.
recipes.notes: Highly versatile; author's favorite Provia recipe. Great for landscapes, still life, street; portraits hit-or-miss. X-Pro3/X100V: use Auto WB instead of Auto White Priority.

image.alt: Baltic Sea – Greve, Denmark – Fujifilm X-T5 – Provia Positive Recipe

recipes.name: CineStill 400D v1
recipes.look: Contrasty, green/yellow-leaning cinematic color-negative look with soft detail and grain.
recipes.notes: Best in sunny daylight, also good on dreary overcast days; pairs well with landscapes. Not for X-T3/X-T30.

recipes.name: CineStill 400D v2
recipes.look: Lower-contrast, red/purple-leaning cinematic film look with soft, dreamy rendering and grain.
recipes.notes: Especially suited to golden hour, also overcast, shade and midday; great for urban/street. Not for X-T3/X-T30.

image.alt: Building Blue – Phoenix, AZ – Fujifilm X-T5

recipes.name: Pushed CineStill 800T
recipes.look: Cool, teal-leaning, gritty pushed-tungsten cinema look with muted tones and heavy grain.
recipes.notes: Good for daytime, especially overcast, and night; use a diffusion filter (10-20% CineBloom suggested) for halation. X-Trans V version; separate X-Trans IV recipe exists.

image.alt: July Bougainvillea – Buckeye, AZ – Fujifilm X-T5 – Pushed CineStill 800T

recipes.name: Expired ECN-2 100T
recipes.look: Odd cross-processed look: teal daylight, green-yellow night casts, gritty grain, muted contrast, experimental lomo feel.
recipes.notes: Unusual, lomo-like; green/yellow cast at night, strong teal cast in daylight. Decent for night; for occasional use. Formerly Patreon early access, now public.

recipes.name: Fluorescent Night
recipes.look: Cool, saturated night-street look with cyan-green fluorescent casts, punchy blues, cinematic urban mood.
recipes.notes: Designed for fluorescent-lit night scenes; also halfway decent in daylight with a cool cast and strong blues. Results vary with bulb types and mixed lighting.

image.alt: Left the Lights On - Buckeye, AZ - Fujifilm X-T5 - Fluorescent Night Recipe

recipes.name: BewareMyVelvia
recipes.look: Hyper-saturated, high-contrast Velvia look with cool-magenta leaning color, vivid and bold, modern slide-film punch.
recipes.notes: Made for multiple exposures, best near/after sunset; also works for single exposures in daylight. Author encourages tweaking.

image.alt: Never be Invisible – Phoenix, AZ – Fujifilm X-T5 - BewareMyVelvia Recipe - Triple Exposure

recipes.name: CineStill 800T
recipes.look: Cool tungsten-balanced night cinema look, teal shadows, soft low-contrast tones, heavy grain, moody neon vibe.
recipes.notes: Great for after-dark photography; sometimes interesting in daylight. Only change from X-Trans IV version is FX Blue Weak. Author calls it an imperfect approximation.

image.alt: Quiet Corner – Tempe, AZ – Fujifilm X-T5 – CineStill 800T

recipes.name: RedScale
recipes.look: Extreme red-orange monochrome-ish cast, ranging yellow to purple; high contrast, gritty, experimental analog.
recipes.notes: Simulates redscale film (exposed through the backing), inspired by Harman Red 125. Niche; not for every situation. Not for X-T3/X-T30.

recipes.name: Vintage Bronze
recipes.look: Warm bronze, desaturated, faded vintage print look with moderate contrast and muted, golden-brown tones.
recipes.notes: Evokes bleach-bypassed motion picture film, cross-processed ColorPlus, or faded vintage Kodacolor. X-Trans IV can use it but renders slightly differently.

image.alt: A Gift For You – Buckeye, AZ – Fujifilm X-T5 – "Vintage Bronze"

recipes.name: Expired Kodak Vision2 250D
recipes.look: Warm, muted, low-saturation expired motion-picture film look with faded amber tones and soft contrast.
recipes.notes: Fun for occasional use if you like warm pictures. D-Range Priority Auto disables Highlight/Shadow. Close but not perfect match to expired film. Formerly Patreon early access.

recipes.name: Vintage Eterna
recipes.look: Warm, contrasty mid-century Kodak color look, cinematic, bright highlights, grainy, retro 1950s-60s.
recipes.notes: Vintage 1950s-60s Kodak color vibe with cinematic quality; pairs well with vintage or characterful lenses. Better for occasional retro use. X-Trans V version extracted.

recipes.name: Vintage Cinema
recipes.look: Warm amber, soft, underexposed cinematic look, bright highlights, muted color, nostalgic 1970s film vibe.
recipes.notes: Best in sunny daylight, especially golden hour; sometimes good in cloudy, shade, indoors. Pairs well with vintage lenses and diffusion filters. Formerly Patron early access.

recipes.name: 1960 Chrome
recipes.look: Vintage 1960s color slide look, muted yet distinct colors, soft highlights, grainy, magazine-print nostalgia.
recipes.notes: Inspired by 1960s Arizona Highways magazine; strong vintage color film aesthetic, shown with landscapes and architecture. GFX may render differently.

image.alt: Bell Tower - Tumacacori, AZ - Fujifilm X-T5 - 1960 Chrome

recipes.name: Eterna Summer
recipes.look: Warm, saturated, cinematic summer look with Kodak-like colors, soft shadows and bright highlights, modern-nostalgic.
recipes.notes: Warm summertime vibes; great for sunny daylight. Cinematic Eterna tonality with Kodak-like colors, inspired by Classic Chrome rather than a specific film.

image.alt: Rock Rings – Saguaro National Park, AZ – Fujifilm X-T5 – Eterna Summer

recipes.name: Ilford FP4 Plus 125
recipes.look: Classic medium-contrast black and white, fine tonality, deep shadows, clean mid-century documentary feel.
recipes.notes: By Anders Lindborg. Best for mid-to-high contrast scenes; underexpose to protect highlights. Clarity/grain tunable (-2 to +4) from soft to gritty.

recipes.name: Kodak Plus-X 125
recipes.look: Classic mid-century black and white, moderate contrast, crisp detail, fine grain, timeless documentary look.
recipes.notes: By Dylan Van Matre, built from Kodak's spectral data and tested for two years. No specific light guidance. Not for X-T3/X-T30.

recipes.name: Kodak T-Max 100 Soft Tone
recipes.look: Smooth, clean modern black and white with soft highlights, fine grain, gentle contrast.
recipes.notes: By Dan Allen; lower-contrast companion to Hard Tone with softer highlights and lifted shadows. Customize to taste.

recipes.name: Kodak T-Max 100 Hard Tone
recipes.look: Crisp, high-contrast modern black and white with deep shadows, fine grain, punchy graphic tones.
recipes.notes: By Dan Allen after shooting T-Max 100 alongside an X-T5; higher-contrast version of the pair (see Soft Tone).

image.alt: Fujifilm X100VI – Kodak T-Max 100 Hard Tone – Photo by Joy Roesch

recipes.name: Kodak T-Max P3200
recipes.look: Gritty, high-contrast, coarse-grained black and white with slight cool tone, pushed-film night/street feel.
recipes.notes: By Anders Lindborg and John Sevigny. Best at ISO 3200-12800; higher ISO mimics push-processing. X-T3/X-T30 usable ignoring toning, grain size, clarity.

recipes.name: Agfa Scala
recipes.look: Bright, high-contrast black-and-white slide look with glowing highlights, deep blacks, crisp fine grain.
recipes.notes: Mimics Agfa Scala 200x slide film: deep blacks, glowing highlights, limited dynamic range. Exposure must be precise; use histogram to avoid overexposure.

image.alt: Faded Highway Shield – Williams, AZ – GFX100RF – Agfa Scala

recipes.name: Classic B&W
recipes.look: Very high-contrast, gritty classic black and white with deep blacks, bright highlights, heavy grain.
recipes.notes: Created on a Manitou Springs photowalk; one of the author's top 5 B&W recipes. Clarity +3 causes a brief Storing pause. Not for X-T3/X-T30.

recipes.name: FRGMT B&W
recipes.look: Punchy, very contrasty, gritty black and white with soft sharpness and heavy grain, pushed-film street look.
recipes.notes: By Hiroshi Fujiwara; creator recommends +1/3 exposure. Clarity +5 causes a storing pause. Resembles Ilford Delta 400 pushed one stop. Not for X-T3/X-T30.

image.alt: Oak Creek in Monochrome – Sedona, AZ – Fujifilm X-E5 – FRGMT B&W

recipes.name: Standard Film
recipes.look: Bright, colorful and slightly warm everyday rendering with a gentle film character.
recipes.notes: Bright, colorful, slightly warm all-rounder; great for landscapes, possibly a bit too vibrant for portraits.

recipes.name: Velvia Film
recipes.look: Punchy, saturated slide-film colors with strong contrast and warm tones.
recipes.notes: For when you want colors to pop, especially landscapes; avoid for portraits as skin can look sunburned.

recipes.name: Astia Summer
recipes.look: Vibrant yet softer summery color with warm, pleasant tones and gentle, film-like contrast.
recipes.notes: Good landscape option when Velvia is too strong; may be too vibrant for portraits.

recipes.name: Kodak Film
recipes.look: Warm Kodak-like negative look with muted richness and pleasing skin tones.
recipes.notes: Versatile across subjects and light, portraits included; similar to Reggie's Portra and expected to be the most popular.

recipes.name: Fujicolor PRO 160C Warm
recipes.look: Warm, natural Fujicolor professional negative colors with gentle contrast and flattering skin tones.
recipes.notes: Versatile, portrait-friendly; the author's favorite of the three PRO-style options.

recipes.name: Superia Negative
recipes.look: Consumer Superia-like negative with warm-cool color contrast and nostalgic snapshot feel.
recipes.notes: Not modeled on a specific Superia stock but has a general Superia Xtra 400 vibe; good everyday option.

recipes.name: Nostalgic Film
recipes.look: Amber-tinted, vibrant retro rendering evoking faded prints from an old family photo album.
recipes.notes: Retro look; possibly slightly too vibrant and amber for portraits.

recipes.name: Neopan Negative
recipes.look: Contrasty, grainy black-and-white reminiscent of Fujifilm Neopan negative film printed on paper.
recipes.notes: Black-and-white; thrives on high-contrast scenes. Set Monochromatic Color off.

recipes.name: Fujicolor PRO Film
recipes.look: Clean, slightly warm professional negative-film colors with moderate contrast and natural saturation.
recipes.notes: Good general and portrait option; author prefers the Reala Ace version.

recipes.name: Fujicolor PRO 160S
recipes.look: Soft, low-contrast professional portrait negative look with gentle, natural colors and smooth skin.
recipes.notes: Author's favorite of the set for pictures of people.

recipes.name: Reduced Bleach
recipes.look: Desaturated, high-contrast bleach-bypass look with a gritty, moody, cinematic feel to scenes.
recipes.notes: For results distinctly different from the other options; gritty and desaturated.

recipes.name: Monochrome Film
recipes.look: Classic grainy black-and-white film look with solid contrast and deep, rich blacks.
recipes.notes: Thrives in high-contrast light; use the color filter options. Set Monochromatic Color off.

recipes.name: Sepia Print
recipes.look: Warm brown-toned monochrome evoking antique sepia prints from a bygone photographic era.
recipes.notes: Niche option for something different; most will skip it.

recipes.name: Universal Provia
recipes.look: Natural, true-to-life color with a subtle Crystal Archive print feel.
recipes.notes: True-to-life with a slight analog vibe. Made for X-Trans V; on X-Trans IV (not X-T3/X-T30) blues render less deep with some sims.

recipes.name: Velvia 100F
recipes.look: Rich, saturated but restrained slide-film color, vivid without looking garish or overdone.
recipes.notes: Colorful but not over-the-top; good for landscapes. Made for X-Trans V; on X-Trans IV (not X-T3/X-T30) blues render less deep with some sims.

recipes.name: Indoor Astia
recipes.look: Soft, warm, gentle color suited to window-lit interiors and quiet everyday indoor scenes.
recipes.notes: Author's favorite of the set for indoor natural light. Made for X-Trans V; on X-Trans IV (not X-T3/X-T30) blues render less deep with some sims.

recipes.name: Elite Chrome
recipes.look: Kodak Elite Chrome-like slide look with deep blues and muted warmth.
recipes.notes: Best in sunny daylight; also fine in overcast and blue hour. Made for X-Trans V; on X-Trans IV (not X-T3/X-T30) blues render less deep with some sims.

recipes.name: Retro Negative
recipes.look: Warm retro color-negative look reminiscent of consumer film from the 1980s and 1990s.
recipes.notes: Excellent for golden hour and blue hour. Made for X-Trans V; on X-Trans IV (not X-T3/X-T30) blues render less deep with some sims.

recipes.name: Fuji Negative
recipes.look: Fujifilm color-negative palette with cool greens, faded shadows, and moderate film-like contrast.
recipes.notes: Favorite of the group for overcast; also good in sun and blue hour. Made for X-Trans V; on X-Trans IV (not X-T3/X-T30) blues render less deep with some sims.

recipes.name: Pulled Negative
recipes.look: Soft, low-contrast pulled-film look with pastel, muted colors and lifted, airy tones.
recipes.notes: Among the best of the set for artificial light. Made for X-Trans V; on X-Trans IV (not X-T3/X-T30) blues render less deep with some sims.

recipes.name: Fujicolor Superia 200
recipes.look: Consumer Superia-style negative with nostalgic tones and teal-magenta color contrast throughout.
recipes.notes: Especially good indoors in natural and artificial light. Made for X-Trans V; on X-Trans IV (not X-T3/X-T30) blues render less deep with some sims.

recipes.name: Americana Film
recipes.look: Warm amber Americana snapshot look with vintage character and nostalgic, sun-faded color.
recipes.notes: Great for portraits or any time you want a retro rendering. Made for X-Trans V; on X-Trans IV (not X-T3/X-T30) blues render less deep with some sims.

recipes.name: Eterna Film
recipes.look: Soft, muted, cinematic motion-picture film color with gentle contrast and grainy texture.
recipes.notes: Soft cinematic quality; great for taming high-contrast scenes. Made for X-Trans V; on X-Trans IV (not X-T3/X-T30) blues render less deep with some sims.

recipes.name: Chrome City
recipes.look: Desaturated, gritty urban look with bold contrast, reminiscent of LomoChrome Metropolis film.
recipes.notes: Can be spectacular; one of the author's favorites, LomoChrome Metropolis-like. Made for X-Trans V; on X-Trans IV (not X-T3/X-T30) blues render less deep with some sims.

recipes.name: Acros Negative
recipes.look: Grainy, film-like Acros black-and-white with soft negative-film tonality and gentle highlights.
recipes.notes: B&W; wonderful in the right situations. Monochromatic Color off. Made for X-Trans V; on X-Trans IV (not X-T3/X-T30) blues render less deep with some sims.

recipes.name: B&W Negative
recipes.look: Grainy classic black-and-white negative look with soft highlights and deep, rich shadows.
recipes.notes: B&W; thrives in high-contrast light, use the filter options. Monochromatic Color off. Made for X-Trans V; on X-Trans IV (not X-T3/X-T30) blues render less deep with some sims.

recipes.name: B&W Sepia
recipes.look: Grainy brown-toned monochrome with soft contrast, evoking vintage sepia prints from long ago.
recipes.notes: For something different. Made for X-Trans V; on X-Trans IV (not X-T3/X-T30) blues render less deep with some sims.

recipes.name: Cinematic Film
recipes.look: Soft, muted cinematic Eterna palette with controlled highlights and a gentle warm cast.
recipes.notes: Tames high-contrast light and suits after-dark shooting. Native X-Trans V recipe; on X-Trans IV set FX Blue to Strong, on newer GFX set Shadow -0.5. Now in the app, but settings are free on the blog.

recipes.name: Kentmere Pan 400
recipes.look: Contrasty, gritty budget black-and-white with heavy large grain and crisp detail.
recipes.notes: Versatile B&W for street, architecture and high-contrast scenes. Identical settings on X-Trans IV (except X-T3/X-T30) and X-Trans V. No Color setting in the post (null).

image.alt: Cash for your Scrap – Buckeye, AZ – Fujifilm X100V – Kentmere Pan 400 – Photo by Jon Roesch

recipes.name: PRO Negative 160C (X-Trans IV & V)
recipes.look: Saturated yet natural, slightly warm colour negative rendering with soft contrast.
recipes.notes: Same settings for X-Trans IV (X-T4 and later) and V; approximates Reala Ace on cameras lacking it. Good for landscapes, architecture, portraits in varied light.

recipes.name: Reggie's Portra
recipes.look: Warm, mid-saturation Portra-style colour with pleasing skin tones and gentle contrast.
recipes.notes: Versatile everyday recipe for most light. Fuji X Weekly's X-Trans V follow-up says it works as-is on X-T5; optionally drop Color Chrome FX Blue to Off for bluer skies to look like X-Trans IV.

image.alt: Dark Clouds Over Lake – Ridgedale, MO – Fujifilm X100V – "Reggie's Portra"

recipes.name: Kodak Tri-X 400
recipes.look: Punchy, gritty classic Tri-X black-and-white with deep shadows and heavy grain.
recipes.notes: Best at ISO 1600+; 6400-12800 evokes older Tri-X. Any Acros filter. No toning setting listed (null). Predates X-Trans V; author notes the app lists it as X-Trans V compatible unchanged.

image.alt: Trolley Bus – Farmington, UT – Fujifilm X100V – ISO 12800 – "Kodak Tri-X 400"

recipes.name: Monochrome Negative
recipes.look: Contrasty monochrome with bright, punchy highlights and a darker, negative-print feel.
recipes.notes: X-Trans IV version used; X-Trans III just drops grain size. Designed for deliberate underexposure. No toning setting given (null). Predates X-Trans V; no V-specific advice.

image.alt: Approaching Storm – Antelope Island SP, UT – Fujifilm X100V

recipes.name: Standard Provia
recipes.look: Clean, true-to-life Provia colour, slightly cool, with soft clarity and bright contrast.
recipes.notes: Good for daytime outdoors and winter landscapes. X-Trans IV post; no X-Trans V advice given. X-T3/X-T30 can substitute a diffusion filter for Clarity.

recipes.name: Ilford HP5 Plus 400
recipes.look: Classic grainy black-and-white with soft highlights, deep shadows and good midtone separation.
recipes.notes: All-day, any-weather B&W; shines in moderate to high contrast. No toning setting listed (null). X-Trans IV post; no X-Trans V advice.

recipes.name: Nostalgic Print
recipes.look: Faded, low-saturation vintage print look, like old snapshots from a cheap point-and-shoot.
recipes.notes: Works for landscapes, plants, street and interiors. X-Trans IV post; no X-Trans V-specific advice given.

appOnly.name: Astia Azure
appOnly.look: Light, bright Astia rendering with rich blue skies; especially nice at golden and blue hour.
appOnly.notes: Early-access; settings only in FXW App for Patrons. Not for X-T3, X-T30, X-Pro3, X100V. No public release found.

appOnly.name: Kodak Gold 200 v3
appOnly.look: Warm consumer-negative film look inspired by Kodak Gold, with a slight green-leaning vintage cast.
appOnly.notes: Early-access; settings only in FXW App for Patrons. Earlier public Kodak Gold 200 recipes exist but are different versions.

appOnly.name: Ektachrome E100
appOnly.look: Vibrant slide-film color with punchy greens and blues, emulating Kodak Ektachrome E100 reversal film.
appOnly.notes: Early-access; settings only in FXW App for Patrons. Still not public over two years later per author comments.

appOnly.name: Fujicolor Blue
appOnly.look: Cool blue-toned retro negative look, like tungsten film shot in daylight or cooling-filtered film.
appOnly.notes: Early-access; settings only in FXW App for Patrons. Author noted a long queue before public release.

appOnly.name: Provia Summer
appOnly.look: Warm, vibrant, colorful summery rendering suited to sunny outdoor scenes.
appOnly.notes: Early-access; settings only in FXW App for Patrons. Author suggested public release sometime in 2026.

appOnly.name: Velvia Slide
appOnly.look: Highly saturated Velvia 100 slide-film look, best for colorful landscapes in bright daylight.
appOnly.notes: Early-access; settings only in FXW App for Patrons. Also compatible with GFX. No public release found.

appOnly.name: Retro Color
appOnly.look: Warm, nostalgic 1960s-70s Ektachrome-like color, strongest in sun and golden hour.
appOnly.notes: Early-access; settings only in FXW App for Patrons. No public release found.

appOnly.name: Astia Negative
appOnly.look: Contrasty, colorful daylight look with a slight blue lean; great for landscapes in warm light.
appOnly.notes: Early-access; settings only in FXW App for Patrons. Also GFX compatible. No public release found.

appOnly.name: 1-Hour Photo
appOnly.look: Warm, saturated yet soft 1980s-90s drugstore print look, like Superia 400 from a one-hour lab.
appOnly.notes: Early-access; settings only in FXW App for Patrons. No public release found.

appOnly.name: Avalon Ace
appOnly.look: Analog Kodak Gold/Portra-like film character, well suited to travel and coastal scenes.
appOnly.notes: Early-access; settings only in FXW App for Patrons. No public release found.
